00:00 Alex Nguyen: Okay everyone thanks for joining. we have about 45 minutes. quick intros? Alex from Redwood, AE. Priya our solutions eng. Marcus from customer success.
00:10 Elena Ruiz: hi, Elena procurement. Dinesh legal. Sofia, head of data. Tom from platform. we maybe have a new person Nina listening in.
00:22 Alex Nguyen: great thanks. high level agenda: confirmation of pilot scope, walk through legal ask (MSA/DPA), security artifacts, basic pricing guidance for procurement, and next steps. anything to add?
00:33 Dinesh Patel: just one, i'd like to flag our DPA clauses around controllers/processors and subprocessor notifications, plus KMS key control.
00:39 Priya Desai: absolutely we'll cover that. quick note: pilot will be sandbox only, no patient PHI, we're happy to run with synthetic or de-identified data.
00:50 Sofia Martinez: that's important — our legal team will still want assurances around logging and retention even with de-identified sets.
00:58 Alex Nguyen: understood. ok pilot scope: we propose a 6-week sandbox pilot, 3 engineers from your side, access to a single dedicated sandbox tenant with limited capacity, run up to X qps for inference, and provide perf metrics. Priya will run perf baselines and a small eval suite.
01:15 Priya Desai: i'll document the exact RPS and seq lengths we expect during the pilot, and propose a configuration for batching and caching so you see cost/latency tradeoffs.
01:26 Tom O'Neill: quick question — for sandbox networking, are you offering VPC peering or do we need to use IP allowlists? our security likes peering.
01:34 Priya Desai: we support both. for Redwood Private (VPC) it's possible to do VPC peering or interconnect; for hosted sandbox we can do IP allowlists. for the pilot i recommend VPC peering to better reflect production network characteristics.
01:48 Tom O'Neill: okay good. any special egress fees or cross-region data transfer we should budget?
01:54 Alex Nguyen: not for the pilot if we keep it within the same cloud region, we'll include the notes in the pricing sheet. production egress depends on your cloud setup.
02:05 Elena Ruiz: procurement — we need to understand the contracting path. do you accept our PO with the MSA attached or do you require signature from your side? what thresholds trigger procurement review?
02:16 Marcus Lee: typically we can accept a PO once MSA terms are agreed; for pilots we often do a Statement of Work (SOW) appended to the MSA. Alex will work with you on the redline.
02:27 Dinesh Patel: on the MSA/DPA we have a few exceptions: vendor must notify subprocessor changes 30 days prior, data deletion on request within 15 days, and we prefer customer-managed KMS.
02:39 Priya Desai: we support KMS integrations; for hosted we integrate with major cloud KMS providers and we have a dedicated private option for customer-managed keys. note that customer-managed KMS may affect some features and performance — we'll surface that in the architecture doc.
02:57 Dinesh Patel: also need to confirm retention windows for logs and whether audit logs will be available for 12 months.
03:04 Alex Nguyen: our standard retention for audit logs in Redwood Hosted is 90 days on the platform, but we have extended retention options as an add-on — we'll put a note in the security packet. Marcus can you flag retention add-on?
03:15 Marcus Lee: noted, will include options and cost impact.
03:19 Sofia Martinez: SOC2 status? and do you have recent penetration tests?
03:23 Alex Nguyen: Redwood has SOC2 Type II, report available under NDA. we also run annual third-party pen tests and internal red team; we can share the latest summary and supporting docs in the secure share.
03:33 Elena Ruiz: can you send those docs to procurement secure mailbox? we can't accept links to public S3 without some access control.
03:40 Alex Nguyen: yes we'll use a time-limited secure share link or transfer via your security contact. Marcus will coordinate.
03:46 Dinesh Patel: on DPA-specific items: subprocessor list and data flow diagrams — those need to be precise. our security team wants to see where tokens and KV caches sit.
03:55 Priya Desai: i'll attach a simplified data flow that shows runtime KV cache behavior, where the model artifacts reside, and options for quantized runtime and local caches. note: some of the infra words may get munged in the auto-transcript, but we'll get precise docs.
04:12 Tom O'Neill: about private deployments — if we move to a Private VPC later, do you have a migration path for model versions and keys?
04:19 Priya Desai: yes we provide model version pinning and can coordinate cross-deployment replication. key migration has to be planned with KMS handoff; we'll create a migration runbook as part of the SOW.
04:30 Elena Ruiz: pricing — what's typical for a 6-week sandbox pilot? we have internal thresholds that require PO above $10k to go through finance. smaller pilots often slip through easier.
04:40 Alex Nguyen: for sandbox pilot we usually offer a discounted fixed-fee pilot package, often in the $7k–12k range depending on capacity and support level. we'll provide a tailored quote with line items (sandbox, SE hours, monitoring).
04:52 Elena Ruiz: fine. we likely need an estimate so procurement can pre-approve the PO path.
04:56 Alex Nguyen: we'll send that week.
04:58 Dinesh Patel: one more legal ask — indemnity and limitation language. we can propose minor redlines but want to avoid expanded liability exposure.
05:07 Alex Nguyen: understood. we try to keep standard liability caps; we'll surface where exceptions are possible.
05:12 Sophia (sic) / Sofia Martinez: sorry, two quick technical points: latency SLOs for inference and whether Redwood provides per-route latency breakdowns during pilot.
05:20 Priya Desai: yes we can enable per-route tracing and token-level latency breakdowns in the Console for the sandbox tenant. SLOs depend on dedicated capacity; hosted sandbox will have best-effort low latency but not SLA. if you want strict SLOs, Dedicated or Private is the path.
05:39 Tom O'Neill: so for the pilot we should expect sub-200ms median for typical gen calls?
05:44 Priya Desai: with small context sequences and moderate batch sizes, median sub-200ms is achievable on optimized models; we'll show baseline numbers.
05:51 Nina: (inaudible)
05:55 Elena Ruiz: procurement question — do you require SSO/SAML for admin access? our policy requires SSO for any vendor console.
06:03 Alex Nguyen: yes we support SAML/SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. we'll include sample metadata and the SSO integration steps.
06:12 Dinesh Patel: also looking for audit log schema and whether you can provide log export to our SIEM via syslog or cloud export.
06:20 Marcus Lee: we offer log export via secure streaming to your cloud storage or SIEM connectors as an add-on. details in the security pack.
06:27 Elena Ruiz: okay great. let's talk decision timeline — procurement wants final numbers and contract by July 24 to submit PO the following week. is that workable?
06:35 Alex Nguyen: yes that's workable if we get DPA/M SA redlines and your PO thresholds this week. we'll aim to get docs out by July 20 so you can escalate internally.
06:45 Dinesh Patel: we will circulate DPA exceptions by July 20.
06:48 Alex Nguyen: perfect. last part — can we recap next steps?

07:13 Elena Ruiz: procurement will confirm PO approvers and threshold by 2026-07-21. Dinesh will send DPA exceptions by 2026-07-20.

07:27 Alex Nguyen: will do. Marcus will open the CRM opportunity and attach the docs.
07:31 Marcus Lee: i'll open the opportunity after the call and invite Aster's procurement/legal contacts.
07:35 Sofia Martinez: any benchmarking we should be aware of? we were evaluating GigaAI for price but their latency looked promising — curious about how Redwood compares on cost per token for similar throughput.
07:47 Alex Nguyen: we ran public benchmarks; cost comparisons depend on model, quantization, and batching. Priya will include an estimate matrix in the pricing sheet and show sensitivity to batching and KV cache hit rates.
07:59 Tom O'Neill: final technical ask — can we get a sample SOW for the pilot so we can see deliverables and acceptance criteria?
08:06 Alex Nguyen: yes, we'll include a draft SOW with acceptance criteria (perf targets, integration checks, security review signoff).
